newsitem.title: USA: US hotel stock offerings fell in H1 1997 -- study.
newsitem.headline: US hotel stock offerings fell in H1 1997 -- study.

text.p: U.S. hotel companies raised fewer dollars in public stock offerings in the first half of 1997 than last year, but hotel real estate investment trusts used the public stock markets to raise more funds, according to a study by Coopers & Lybrand LLC.

Lodging firms raised $1.2 billion in public stock offerings in the first half of 1997, down from $2 billion last year, the study said. But hotel real estate investment trusts (REITs) raised about a billion dollars, up from last year's $732 million.

Bjorn Hanson, the chairman of Coopers & Lybrand's lodging practice noted that the IPO market in general was slower in the first half of 1997 than it was in the first half of 1996, when demand for new stock was at "tremendous" levels.
He also said many lodging firms went public between 1994 and 1996, leaving few to raise money through IPOs this year.

In the second quarter, lodging corporations raised $300 million, sharply below the $1.5 billion raised last year. Lodging REITs raised $534 million, down from the $732 million raised in the year-ago period, but more than the $488.5 million generated in the first quarter of 1997.
In the second quarter, three hotel companies raised money in stock offerings with secondary offerings by Servico Inc and Bristol Hotel Co and a $56 million IPO by Silverleaf Resorts Inc.
Three hotel REITs held secondary offerings, FelCor Suite Hotels Inc, Equity Inns Inc, and Sunstone Hotel Investors Inc.
The study was compiled by the Lodging Research Network, (www.lodgingresearch.com), created by Hanson.
